itemListElement.name: Jamie AI Note Taker Review: A 2026 Look for US Teams

mainEntity.name: Is the Jamie AI note taker free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Jamie's free plan includes 10 AI notes a month, each up to 30 minutes long, and paid plans start at $24 for Plus. That 30-minute cap is the main limit, so a 45-minute client call gets cut off. Short check-ins and testing suit it better than daily use.

mainEntity.name: How much does Jamie AI cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Jamie Plus costs $24, Pro costs $46 a month billed yearly, and Team costs $37 per seat per month billed yearly. Enterprise pricing is custom, and monthly billing is available through a toggle on Jamie's pricing page. Pro is the first plan with unlimited notes and 5-hour meetings.

mainEntity.name: Does Jamie join meetings as a bot?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Jamie records audio from your device, so no bot appears in Zoom, Google Meet or Teams. Attendees still need to be told the meeting is being recorded. Because nothing joins the call, it works with almost any meeting app. The catch: you must start it yourself, so missed starts mean missed notes.

Yes, in beta. Jamie offers an iOS app and a beta Android app for in-person meetings, while desktop apps handle online meetings. Because the Android app is a beta, features may lag the iPhone version. Test it on a real in-person meeting before relying on it.

Jamie lists notes and transcripts in 99+ languages on its pricing page. Speaker recognition and task detection are included on every plan. Data is hosted in the EU, and Jamie states it does not train models on your data, which suits teams with European clients or strict privacy rules.

mainEntity.name: What is a good alternative to Jamie?

acceptedAnswer.text: Granola offers bot-free notes for $14 a month, Fathom offers unlimited free recording, and Lynkk offers bot or bot-free capture plus prep, live answers and Jira tickets for $15 a month.
